cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a man's hand-woven strip-cloth cotton gown (boubou/tobe) with hand-sewn embroidered figures, a garment type widely worn across the West African Sahel including by Wolof men, and consistent with the claimed category and ethnicity.

physical.title: gown; textile; tobe
physical.summary: Man’s gown (boubou, tobe) formed from 66 narrow strips hand-woven and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. Both the body and sleeves of the gown are formed from uniform strips of cotton of equal length: the body is made of strips sewn vertically, while the sleeves are sewn horizontally. The cotton in these strips is entirely hand-spun and buff in colour, and is woven in plain-weave without decoration in either warp or weft. Over the entire front of the gown embroidered decoration has been added by hand-sewing figures (of animals, reptiles and a human seen at the left) or abstract patterns (seen in the centre and right); these are all in European white, blue and pink cotton. Around the neck have been couched down two arcs cut from a red cloth of European origin. The cut ends at the openings have sewn hems.
